+//! The Perfetto encoder: [`TraceEvent`]s in, a binary `.perfetto-trace` out.
+//!
+//! What a Collection looks like in a trace is decided in [`crate::monitor::convert`], as it is
+//! for Chrome. This file knows only how Perfetto spells a trace: which field number carries
+//! what, and that a track has to be declared before an event names it.
+//!
+//! ## What it writes today
+//!
+//! The clock snapshot, the root descriptor, one track per process and one per interpreter under
+//! it, the marker that keeps a process visible when it never collects, a slice per Collection and
+//! per sub-phase, and every metric series as a counter track of its own under a `GC Metrics`
+//! heading. Only [`TraceEvent::Instant`] is still dropped, and nothing produces one. The encoding
+//! machinery was checked against a decoder gcscope did not write before any layout policy rode on
+//! it ([ADR 0021](../../../docs/adr/0021-hand-rolled-perfetto-encoder.md)).
+//!
+//! ## Which clock
+//!
+//! One, and the trace says which ([ADR
+//! 0022](../../../docs/adr/0022-every-timestamp-names-its-clock.md)). A Collection's timestamps
+//! are what CPython published, on the machine's monotonic clock; gcscope reads that same clock
+//! for itself ([`crate::monitor::clock`]), so an Observer reading is a point in the same domain
+//! rather than a domain of its own. Every packet carrying a timestamp names that domain, and one
+//! [`ClockSnapshot`](clock_snapshot_packet) ties it to the clock Perfetto measures trace time in.
+//! The numbers CPython published reach the file unchanged; the conversion is the reader's.
+//!
+//! ## The shape of the file
+//!
+//! A `Trace` is a repeated `TracePacket` and carries no header, length or index. The file is
+//! therefore the concatenation of its packets, each written as one length-delimited `packet`
+//! field, and an encoder can append as it goes and stop anywhere — a trace truncated by a
+//! crash is the prefix that was written, still readable.
+
+use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
+use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
+use std::io::Write;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+use super::perfetto_proto::{
+    builtin_clock, child_tracks_ordering, clock, clock_snapshot, counter_descriptor,
+    debug_annotation, process_descriptor, process_ordering, thread_ordering, trace, trace_packet,
+    track_descriptor, track_event, track_event_type,
+};
+use super::protobuf::{put_double, put_int32, put_int64, put_message, put_string, put_uint64};
+use super::{EventsExporter, ProcessLifecycle};
+use crate::monitor::clock::RunClock;
+use crate::monitor::trace_event::{Arg, ArgValue, TraceEvent};
+
+/// The extension a Perfetto trace takes, and what [`EventsExporter::output_path`] resolves an
+/// operator's `--output` to. `ui.perfetto.dev` reads a trace by content rather than by name,
+/// so this is for the operator: a `.json` holding protobuf is a file nobody can open twice.
+pub const EXTENSION: &str = "perfetto-trace";
+
+/// The track every top-level descriptor is ordered under. Perfetto reserves uuid 0 for it.
+const ROOT_TRACK_UUID: u64 = 0;
+
+/// The first uuid handed out to a real track. Anything but 0, which the root holds.
+const FIRST_TRACK_UUID: u64 = 1;
+
+/// Every packet gcscope writes belongs to one sequence, and a trace has exactly one producer,
+/// so the id is a constant rather than a value drawn from the address of something. Perfetto
+/// drops packets that name no sequence at all — interning and incremental state are
+/// sequence-scoped — and a fixed value keeps two runs of the same input byte-identical.
+const SEQUENCE_ID: u64 = 1;
+
+/// What the marker that keeps a silent process visible is called.
+const START_PROCESS: &str = "Start Process";
+
+/// What the metric tracks are gathered under, one per interpreter.
+const COUNTER_GROUP_NAME: &str = "GC Metrics";
+
+/// The order the metric tracks read in, and the only thing that decides it.
+///
+/// Ranked by **metric rather than by series**, so the three generations' `collected` tracks sit
+/// together and an operator reading one against another finds them adjacent — which is the same
+/// reason they share a Y axis. Within a metric the order is the order the generations were met.
+const METRIC_ORDER: &[&str] = &[
+    "heap_size",
+    "collections",
+    "collected",
+    "uncollectable",
+    "candidates",
+    "duration",
+];
+
+/// The metrics that describe the interpreter rather than one of its generations, and so are
+/// drawn beside the group instead of inside it.
+///
+/// The heap is the interpreter's, and every generation's Record republishes the same figure. Left
+/// in the grouping it reads as one generation's, which is a claim about the target that is not
+/// true; promoted, it is one track where a whole-heap figure belongs.
+const TOP_LEVEL_METRICS: &[&str] = &["heap_size"];
+
+/// Where the group sits among an interpreter's own tracks: after the metrics promoted out of it.
+const COUNTER_GROUP_RANK: i32 = TOP_LEVEL_METRICS.len() as i32;
+
+/// Where one metric's track sorts among its siblings.
+///
+/// A metric nobody ranked sorts after every one someone chose. Folding it in with the first
+/// instead — which is what a `0` default does — would put a new field silently at the top.
+fn metric_rank(metric: &str) -> i32 {
+    METRIC_ORDER
+        .iter()
+        .position(|known| *known == metric)
+        .unwrap_or(METRIC_ORDER.len()) as i32
+}
+
+/// Whether this metric is drawn beside the group rather than in it.
+fn is_top_level(metric: &str) -> bool {
+    TOP_LEVEL_METRICS.contains(&metric)
+}
+
+/// What one component of a series is called on its own track.
+///
+/// A series names its components: `G0` and `collected` make `G0 collected`. A single-component
+/// series carries an empty name and takes its label from the argument key alone, which is the
+/// rule [`TraceEvent::Counter`] states and this only spells.
+fn counter_label(series: &str, metric: &str) -> String {
+    if series.is_empty() {
+        metric.to_string()
+    } else {
+        format!("{series} {metric}")
+    }
+}
+
+/// gcscope's clock domain: the machine's monotonic counter, the one CPython times a Collection
+/// with. Perfetto keeps 1..=63 for the clocks it knows itself
+/// ([`builtin_clock::MAX_ID`]) and reads 64..=127 as scoped to the sequence that declared them,
+/// which is exactly what this is — gcscope writes one sequence, and the snapshot naming this id
+/// travels on it.
+const GCSCOPE_CLOCK_ID: u32 = 64;
+
+/// One `TracePacket`, framed as the `Trace.packet` field that holds it.
+fn packet(body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut out = Vec::new();
+    put_message(&mut out, trace::PACKET, body);
+    out
+}
+
+/// A packet carrying one `TrackDescriptor`.
+///
+/// Fields go out in ascending number, which is protobuf's canonical order and not something
+/// the format requires. It is a decision so that one input produces one byte sequence.
+fn descriptor_packet(descriptor: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut body = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut body,
+        trace_packet::TRUSTED_PACKET_SEQUENCE_ID,
+        SEQUENCE_ID,
+    );
+    put_message(&mut body, trace_packet::TRACK_DESCRIPTOR, descriptor);
+    packet(&body)
+}
+
+/// A packet carrying one `TrackEvent` at `ts_ns` on gcscope's clock domain.
+///
+/// The timestamp goes on the **packet**, never inside the `TrackEvent`: field 1 there is
+/// `timestamp_delta_us`, so an absolute nanosecond stamp written into the event decodes as a
+/// microsecond delta and lands somewhere else entirely. That mistake cost gcmon a shipped bug
+/// and is the reason `trace_packet::TIMESTAMP` carries the warning it does.
+///
+/// The domain is named on every one of these rather than left to the trace's default, which is
+/// BOOTTIME — a claim gcscope cannot make about a counter it read out of CPython.
+fn event_packet(ts_ns: u64, event: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut body = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut body, trace_packet::TIMESTAMP, ts_ns);
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut body,
+        trace_packet::TRUSTED_PACKET_SEQUENCE_ID,
+        SEQUENCE_ID,
+    );
+    put_message(&mut body, trace_packet::TRACK_EVENT, event);
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut body,
+        trace_packet::TIMESTAMP_CLOCK_ID,
+        u64::from(GCSCOPE_CLOCK_ID),
+    );
+    packet(&body)
+}
+
+/// The packet that makes every other timestamp in the trace mean something.
+///
+/// It publishes one instant twice: on the clock gcscope stamps its packets with, and on the one
+/// Perfetto measures trace time in. Without it a reader has no path from gcscope's domain to its
+/// own, and trace-processor does not fall back to guessing — it reports
+/// `clock_sync_failure_no_path` and **drops every event**. That is also why the second reading is
+/// BOOTTIME and not the more obvious MONOTONIC or REALTIME: those were tried, and both leave the
+/// same gap ([ADR 0022](../../../docs/adr/0022-every-timestamp-names-its-clock.md)).
+///
+/// `primary_trace_clock` is left unset, so trace time stays the default, which is the BOOTTIME
+/// this anchors against.
+fn clock_snapshot_packet(run: &RunClock) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut boot = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut boot,
+        clock::CLOCK_ID,
+        u64::from(builtin_clock::BOOTTIME),
+    );
+    put_uint64(&mut boot, clock::TIMESTAMP, run.boottime_ns());
+
+    let mut monotonic = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut monotonic, clock::CLOCK_ID, u64::from(GCSCOPE_CLOCK_ID));
+    // A monotonic reading is never negative on any platform gcscope runs on, and a wrapped one
+    // would place the whole trace 584 years out rather than fail — so it is clamped rather than
+    // cast.
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut monotonic,
+        clock::TIMESTAMP,
+        u64::try_from(run.monotonic_ns()).unwrap_or(0),
+    );
+
+    let mut snapshot = Vec::new();
+    put_message(&mut snapshot, clock_snapshot::CLOCKS, &boot);
+    put_message(&mut snapshot, clock_snapshot::CLOCKS, &monotonic);
+
+    let mut body = Vec::new();
+    put_message(&mut body, trace_packet::CLOCK_SNAPSHOT, &snapshot);
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut body,
+        trace_packet::TRUSTED_PACKET_SEQUENCE_ID,
+        SEQUENCE_ID,
+    );
+    packet(&body)
+}
+
+/// The uuid-0 root descriptor.
+///
+/// **This is what makes explicit process and thread ordering possible at all.** The
+/// `sibling_order_rank` on a top-level process or thread track is honoured only when the root
+/// track says the ordering is explicit, so every later descriptor that wants a place in the
+/// tree hangs off this one packet. It carries no name and no `process`/`thread`/`counter`
+/// sub-message, so trace-processor does not surface it as a track row.
+///
+/// The hints are written unconditionally, with no version gate: a reader that does not
+/// understand them ignores them and falls back to its own ordering, so the trace is
+/// forward-compatible and nothing is lost on an older one.
+fn root_descriptor() -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut descriptor = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::UUID, ROOT_TRACK_UUID);
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut descriptor,
+        track_descriptor::PROCESS_ORDERING,
+        u64::from(process_ordering::EXPLICIT),
+    );
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut descriptor,
+        track_descriptor::THREAD_ORDERING,
+        u64::from(thread_ordering::EXPLICIT),
+    );
+    descriptor_packet(&descriptor)
+}
+
+/// A top-level track for one process.
+///
+/// The `name` is the track's title and `process.process_name` is what the query engine reports
+/// in its `process` table. Both, because they are separate fields answering separate questions
+/// and a reader looking for one does not find the other.
+///
+/// `rank` orders this process against its siblings, honoured because the root descriptor said
+/// the ordering is explicit. Without it the tree reads in whatever order gcscope happened to
+/// see the processes in, which is a property of the poll rather than of the program.
+///
+/// **No `start_timestamp_ns`.** The field wants the moment the process began, on the target's
+/// clock, and gcscope has no reading on that clock — it attached partway through a program
+/// already running. Writing the attach instead would date a process to when it was noticed
+/// ([ADR 0022](../../../docs/adr/0022-every-timestamp-names-its-clock.md)).
+///
+/// `ProcessDescriptor.pid` is an `int32`, so a pid that does not fit one cannot be spelled in
+/// this format; the cast wraps rather than inventing a substitute. No OS gcscope attaches on
+/// issues pids that large.
+fn process_track(uuid: u64, pid: u32, name: Option<&str>, rank: i32) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut process = Vec::new();
+    put_int32(&mut process, process_descriptor::PID, pid as i32);
+    if let Some(name) = name {
+        put_string(&mut process, process_descriptor::PROCESS_NAME, name);
+    }
+
+    let mut descriptor = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::UUID, uuid);
+    if let Some(name) = name {
+        put_string(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::NAME, name);
+    }
+    put_message(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::PROCESS, &process);
+    // A child's `sibling_order_rank` counts only where its **parent** says the ordering is
+    // explicit, the same bargain the root descriptor strikes for the process tracks under it.
+    // Without this the ranks on the interpreter tracks are inert and Perfetto falls back to its
+    // own rule. Written unconditionally: a reader that does not understand the hint ignores it.
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut descriptor,
+        track_descriptor::CHILD_ORDERING,
+        u64::from(child_tracks_ordering::EXPLICIT),
+    );
+    put_int32(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::SIBLING_ORDER_RANK, rank);
+    descriptor_packet(&descriptor)
+}
+
+/// A track for one interpreter, hanging off its process's.
+///
+/// **No `thread` sub-message, and that is the whole decision here.** gcscope draws one track per
+/// interpreter, and an interpreter id is not an OS thread id — a `ThreadDescriptor` would put it
+/// in trace-processor's `thread` table as a thread with that tid, which is a claim about the
+/// target that is not true and which collides with a real thread of that number the day this
+/// trace is merged with anything else. A plain child track says only what gcscope knows: this
+/// belongs to that process, and it is called this. Perfetto also ignores `sibling_order_rank` on
+/// OS-scoped tracks, so the rank below would have been a no-op on one.
+///
+/// `rank` is the order gcscope met the interpreters within this process, so the tree reads the
+/// way the program ran rather than the way a poll happened to return.
+fn interpreter_track(uuid: u64, parent_uuid: u64, name: Option<&str>, rank: i32) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut descriptor = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::UUID, uuid);
+    if let Some(name) = name {
+        put_string(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::NAME, name);
+    }
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::PARENT_UUID, parent_uuid);
+    // The same bargain the process track strikes for this one: a child's rank counts only where
+    // its parent says the ordering is explicit, and the metric tracks below this are children.
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut descriptor,
+        track_descriptor::CHILD_ORDERING,
+        u64::from(child_tracks_ordering::EXPLICIT),
+    );
+    put_int32(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::SIBLING_ORDER_RANK, rank);
+    descriptor_packet(&descriptor)
+}
+
+/// The heading the metric tracks are gathered under, one per interpreter.
+///
+/// **A plain track, scoped to neither a process nor a thread, and that is what it is for.**
+/// trace-processor ignores `sibling_order_rank` on an OS-scoped track, so metric tracks hung
+/// straight off a process descriptor come out in whatever order the encoder happened to write
+/// them and no hint can move them. A group scoped to neither is the workaround: the ranks on its
+/// children count, and the operator gets the order somebody chose. Written without that sentence
+/// it is a mystery, which is why the sentence is here.
+///
+/// It hangs off the **interpreter's** track rather than the process's, unlike gcmon's, and for a
+/// reason that is gcscope's own: gcscope draws its per-interpreter track as a plain child track
+/// too, so there is a level here that gcmon's OS-scoped thread tracks could not offer. Under the
+/// process, a tree with sub-interpreters would carry one identically-named `GC Metrics` heading
+/// per interpreter with nothing telling them apart.
+fn counter_group_track(uuid: u64, parent_uuid: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut descriptor = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::UUID, uuid);
+    put_string(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::NAME, COUNTER_GROUP_NAME);
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::PARENT_UUID, parent_uuid);
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut descriptor,
+        track_descriptor::CHILD_ORDERING,
+        u64::from(child_tracks_ordering::EXPLICIT),
+    );
+    put_int32(
+        &mut descriptor,
+        track_descriptor::SIBLING_ORDER_RANK,
+        COUNTER_GROUP_RANK,
+    );
+    descriptor_packet(&descriptor)
+}
+
+/// One metric's track.
+///
+/// The `counter` sub-message is what makes it a counter track at all, so it is written even when
+/// there is nothing to put in it: an *empty* sub-message is a field that is present and says
+/// nothing, which is different from a field nobody wrote.
+///
+/// `share_key` is what puts `G0 collected` and `G2 collected` on one Y axis instead of at two
+/// scales an operator cannot read against each other. Only tracks with the same parent can share
+/// one, which is the other half of what the group is for — and why a metric promoted out of the
+/// group carries no key: alone at its level, it has nobody to share with, and a key claiming
+/// otherwise would be a scale nothing else is drawn to.
+fn counter_track(
+    uuid: u64,
+    parent_uuid: u64,
+    name: &str,
+    rank: i32,
+    share_key: Option<&str>,
+) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut counter = Vec::new();
+    if let Some(share_key) = share_key {
+        put_string(
+            &mut counter,
+            counter_descriptor::Y_AXIS_SHARE_KEY,
+            share_key,
+        );
+    }
+
+    let mut descriptor = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::UUID, uuid);
+    put_string(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::NAME, name);
+    put_uint64(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::PARENT_UUID, parent_uuid);
+    put_message(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::COUNTER, &counter);
+    put_int32(&mut descriptor, track_descriptor::SIBLING_ORDER_RANK, rank);
+    descriptor_packet(&descriptor)
+}
+
+/// One sample of one metric.
+///
+/// The kinds are kept apart here as they are on a slice's annotations: a count goes to
+/// `counter_value` and `duration`, which is a float of seconds, to `double_counter_value`. The
+/// two share a `oneof`, so writing both would leave only the second — and a duration rounded into
+/// an integer counter loses everything below a whole second, which for a young run is all of it.
+///
+/// **What a sample means is the Record's, not this encoder's.** `duration` is a Lifetime total of
+/// GC seconds, the same shape as `collections` and `collected` — [`crate::monitor::loss`]
+/// differences it for exactly that reason — so the track it draws climbs rather than tracing
+/// pause lengths, and `candidates` beside it is per-Collection. Renaming either here is the one
+/// thing that must not happen: what a figure is called is [`crate::monitor::convert`]'s, decided
+/// once so the two formats describe one run the same way.
+fn counter_sample(uuid: u64, ts_ns: u64, value: ArgValue) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut event = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut event,
+        track_event::TYPE,
+        u64::from(track_event_type::COUNTER),
+    );
+    put_uint64(&mut event, track_event::TRACK_UUID, uuid);
+    match value {
+        ArgValue::Int(v) => put_int64(&mut event, track_event::COUNTER_VALUE, v),
+        ArgValue::Float(v) => put_double(&mut event, track_event::DOUBLE_COUNTER_VALUE, v),
+    }
+    event_packet(ts_ns, &event)
+}
+
+/// One event argument as a debug annotation.
+///
+/// The kinds are kept apart: an `Int` goes to `int_value` and a `Float` to `double_value`,
+/// rather than both to `string_value`. That is what lets a reader sum a count or plot a duration
+/// in trace-processor instead of parsing text back into a number — and what makes `duration`,
+/// which is a float of seconds, survive the trip as one.
+///
+/// `name` is field **10**, not field 1. Field 1 of that `oneof` is the interned id, so a string
+/// written there decodes as a garbage IID; see [`debug_annotation::NAME`].
+fn annotation(&(key, value): &Arg) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut out = Vec::new();
+    match value {
+        ArgValue::Int(v) => put_int64(&mut out, debug_annotation::INT_VALUE, v),
+        ArgValue::Float(v) => put_double(&mut out, debug_annotation::DOUBLE_VALUE, v),
+    }
+    put_string(&mut out, debug_annotation::NAME, key);
+    out
+}
+
+/// The opening half of a slice: what it is called, what it is categorised as, and everything the
+/// conversion decided to carry with it.
+///
+/// The name, the category and the argument keys all come from
+/// [`crate::monitor::convert`]. Nothing is renamed on the way out, so the two formats describe
+/// one run the same way — which is the whole reason that conversion is not per format.
+fn slice_begin(uuid: u64, ts_ns: u64, name: &str, cat: &str, args: &[Arg]) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut event = Vec::new();
+    for arg in args {
+        put_message(&mut event, track_event::DEBUG_ANNOTATIONS, &annotation(arg));
+    }
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut event,
+        track_event::TYPE,
+        u64::from(track_event_type::SLICE_BEGIN),
+    );
+    put_uint64(&mut event, track_event::TRACK_UUID, uuid);
+    put_string(&mut event, track_event::CATEGORIES, cat);
+    put_string(&mut event, track_event::NAME, name);
+    event_packet(ts_ns, &event)
+}
+
+/// The closing half: the track, and that it closes.
+///
+/// **A `SLICE_END` carries no name and no category** — Perfetto closes whatever is innermost on
+/// the track. So the name and category an [`TraceEvent::End`] repeats have nowhere to go on the
+/// wire, and the only thing an encoder can do with them is check them, which is exactly why the
+/// event model repeats them.
+fn slice_end(uuid: u64, ts_ns: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut event = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut event,
+        track_event::TYPE,
+        u64::from(track_event_type::SLICE_END),
+    );
+    put_uint64(&mut event, track_event::TRACK_UUID, uuid);
+    event_packet(ts_ns, &event)
+}
+
+/// The zero-duration instant that makes a process's track visible.
+///
+/// **Perfetto's UI hides a track with no events on it.** A process that never collects has no
+/// events at all, so without this marker the operator's worker is missing from the trace they
+/// opened to find out whether it collected — and "it did none" is a different answer from "it
+/// is not there". One per process, on the process track itself.
+///
+/// The timestamp is when gcscope attached, not anything the target did — but it is on the same
+/// clock a Collection's is, so the marker and the first slice after it sit where they belong
+/// against each other. It used to carry a `clock` annotation saying which clock in prose; the
+/// domain on the packet says it in a form a reader can convert, and a second statement that
+/// cannot go stale in step with the first is worse than none
+/// ([ADR 0022](../../../docs/adr/0022-every-timestamp-names-its-clock.md)).
+fn start_process_instant(uuid: u64, ts_ns: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
+    let mut event = Vec::new();
+    put_uint64(
+        &mut event,
+        track_event::TYPE,
+        u64::from(track_event_type::INSTANT),
+    );
+    put_uint64(&mut event, track_event::TRACK_UUID, uuid);
+    put_string(&mut event, track_event::NAME, START_PROCESS);
+    event_packet(ts_ns, &event)
+}
+
+/// A slice this exporter has opened on a track and not yet closed.
+///
+/// `name` and `cat` are kept only to check the [`TraceEvent::End`] that closes it against them;
+/// neither reaches the wire, because a `SLICE_END` carries no name.
+struct OpenSlice {
+    name: String,
+    cat: String,
+    /// Whether the opening half reached the file. A begin gcscope could not write must not be
+    /// closed by an end that does, or the end closes whatever is under it instead.
+    written: bool,
+}
+
+pub struct PerfettoExporter {
+    file: Option<File>,
+    /// Where the run began on the machine's clock, and the same instant on Perfetto's. Held
+    /// rather than read per event: an anchor that moved would be a second, disagreeing claim
+    /// about where the trace sits.
+    run: RunClock,
+    /// The track declared for each process, so a second event from one pid does not declare it
+    /// again. Like Chrome's metadata dedup, this belongs to the output stream rather than to
+    /// the conversion: a reopened file needs its descriptors written again.
+    process_tracks: HashMap<u32, u64>,
+    /// What each process is called, kept apart from the track it names. The announcement that
+    /// carries a name arrives once per process, so a descriptor written *without* one — a start
+    /// mark that beat the announcement, or a first write that failed and was retried — would be
+    /// nameless for the rest of the run if the name were not held here. Survives `open`, since
+    /// a reopened file re-declares the same tracks and wants the same names.
+    process_names: HashMap<u32, String>,
+    /// Processes whose visibility marker has gone out. Idempotent per process, and kept apart
+    /// from `process_tracks` because the two are set by different signals: the announcement
+    /// declares a track without marking it, and a second start mark for one process must not
+    /// draw a second marker.
+    marked_started: HashSet<u32>,
+    /// The track declared for each interpreter, keyed by the process it belongs to and the id a
+    /// [`TraceEvent`] carries as `tid`.
+    interpreter_tracks: HashMap<(u32, i64), u64>,
+    /// What each interpreter's track is called, kept apart from the track for the same reason
+    /// the process names are: the announcement naming it arrives once, and a track declared
+    /// before it — or after a write that failed — would otherwise stay nameless for the run.
+    interpreter_names: HashMap<(u32, i64), String>,
+    /// The heading each interpreter's metric tracks hang off, declared on the first sample that
+    /// needs one. An interpreter whose only metrics are promoted out of the group never draws it.
+    counter_groups: HashMap<(u32, i64), u64>,
+    /// The track each metric of each series is drawn on, keyed by the interpreter that published
+    /// it, the series it belongs to and the metric itself. The series is part of the key because
+    /// `G0 collected` and `G1 collected` are two tracks; the metric is, because one series draws
+    /// one track per component.
+    counter_tracks: HashMap<(u32, i64, String, &'static str), u64>,
+    /// The slices open on each track, innermost last. Keyed by track uuid rather than by
+    /// `(pid, tid)`, because nesting is a property of the track Perfetto closes against.
+    open_slices: HashMap<u64, Vec<OpenSlice>>,
+    /// How many `End`s did not match what was open. A count rather than a flag, so a run says
+    /// how much of its trace it distrusts rather than only that something was wrong: the first
+    /// is named as it happens and the total reported at `close`.
+    mismatched_ends: usize,
+    /// How many readings could not be placed on this timeline, counted the same way and for the
+    /// same reason: the events this format had to drop and the Chrome trace of the same run kept.
+    unplaceable: usize,
+    next_uuid: u64,
+}
+
+/// Hand-written rather than derived, for two fields. A derived `Default` starts `next_uuid` at
+/// `0`, the uuid the root descriptor holds — `open` sets it too, so the derive would be wrong
+/// only in a window nothing reaches today, which is exactly the kind of invariant that stops
+/// holding when someone adds a call site. And the anchor is a reading of the machine, which
+/// nothing can derive.
+impl Default for PerfettoExporter {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        Self::with_clock(crate::monitor::clock::run_clock())
+    }
+}
+
+impl PerfettoExporter {
+    pub fn new() -> Self {
+        Self::default()
+    }
+
+    /// An exporter anchored to a stated instant rather than to now.
+    ///
+    /// For the tests that pin bytes: a real anchor is two live readings, so a trace built on one
+    /// is never twice the same and a byte-for-byte gate over it could only ever be regenerated.
+    pub fn with_clock(run: RunClock) -> Self {
+        Self {
+            file: None,
+            run,
+            process_tracks: HashMap::new(),
+            process_names: HashMap::new(),
+            marked_started: HashSet::new(),
+            interpreter_tracks: HashMap::new(),
+            interpreter_names: HashMap::new(),
+            counter_groups: HashMap::new(),
+            counter_tracks: HashMap::new(),
+            open_slices: HashMap::new(),
+            mismatched_ends: 0,
+            unplaceable: 0,
+            next_uuid: FIRST_TRACK_UUID,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Declare a track for `pid` if it has none, and return its uuid.
+    ///
+    /// The name comes from whatever the announcement left in `process_names`, so a track
+    /// declared by something that does not carry one — a lifecycle mark arriving first — still
+    /// gets the name once it is known. A track declared before any announcement is nameless
+    /// rather than named a guess, and the pid still identifies it.
+    ///
+    /// A pid is recorded as declared only *after* its descriptor reaches the file. Recording it
+    /// first means a failed write is never retried: the run then finishes reporting a trace
+    /// written, and every later event naming that uuid sits on a track nothing declared.
+    fn track_for(&mut self, pid: u32) -> Option<u64> {
+        if let Some(uuid) = self.process_tracks.get(&pid) {
+            return Some(*uuid);
+        }
+        let uuid = self.next_uuid;
+        // The rank is the order gcscope met the processes, which for a tree is the target and
+        // then its workers as they appeared. Assigned as each is declared rather than sorted at
+        // the end, because this encoder writes as it goes and never rewrites a descriptor.
+        let rank = self.process_tracks.len() as i32;
+        let descriptor = process_track(
+            uuid,
+            pid,
+            self.process_names.get(&pid).map(String::as_str),
+            rank,
+        );
+
+        self.file.as_mut()?.write_all(&descriptor).ok()?;
+        self.next_uuid += 1;
+        self.process_tracks.insert(pid, uuid);
+        Some(uuid)
+    }
+
+    /// Declare a track for one interpreter of `pid` if it has none, and return its uuid.
+    ///
+    /// The process's track comes first, because this one hangs off it — a `parent_uuid` naming a
+    /// track nobody declared is what the harness's checks reject.
+    ///
+    /// Recorded only once its descriptor reaches the file, for the same reason as
+    /// [`track_for`](Self::track_for).
+    fn interpreter_track_for(&mut self, pid: u32, tid: i64) -> Option<u64> {
+        if let Some(uuid) = self.interpreter_tracks.get(&(pid, tid)) {
+            return Some(*uuid);
+        }
+        let parent = self.track_for(pid)?;
+
+        let uuid = self.next_uuid;
+        // Ranked within the process, so two processes each start at zero and neither is ordered
+        // against the other's interpreters.
+        let rank = self
+            .interpreter_tracks
+            .keys()
+            .filter(|(owner, _)| *owner == pid)
+            .count() as i32;
+        let descriptor = interpreter_track(
+            uuid,
+            parent,
+            self.interpreter_names.get(&(pid, tid)).map(String::as_str),
+            rank,
+        );
+
+        self.file.as_mut()?.write_all(&descriptor).ok()?;
+        self.next_uuid += 1;
+        self.interpreter_tracks.insert((pid, tid), uuid);
+        Some(uuid)
+    }
+
+    /// Declare the heading this interpreter's metric tracks hang off, if it has none.
+    ///
+    /// The interpreter's own track comes first, because this one hangs off it. Recorded only
+    /// once its descriptor reaches the file, for the same reason as [`track_for`](Self::track_for).
+    fn counter_group_for(&mut self, pid: u32, tid: i64) -> Option<u64> {
+        if let Some(uuid) = self.counter_groups.get(&(pid, tid)) {
+            return Some(*uuid);
+        }
+        let parent = self.interpreter_track_for(pid, tid)?;
+
+        let uuid = self.next_uuid;
+        let descriptor = counter_group_track(uuid, parent);
+
+        self.file.as_mut()?.write_all(&descriptor).ok()?;
+        self.next_uuid += 1;
+        self.counter_groups.insert((pid, tid), uuid);
+        Some(uuid)
+    }
+
+    /// Declare the track one metric of one series is drawn on, if it has none.
+    ///
+    /// Where it hangs is the layout decision: a metric describing the interpreter goes beside the
+    /// group, everything else inside it. Only what sits inside carries a share key, since sharing
+    /// an axis is a claim about siblings.
+    ///
+    /// The key is built before the lookup, so a hit — which is every sample after the first —
+    /// allocates one `String`. Kept, deliberately: it is a handful per poll on a path that has
+    /// just read another process's memory, and the alternative is a two-level map scanned
+    /// linearly, which is more code for a cost nobody has measured. Performance here is guarded
+    /// by a trigger and a pre-chosen instrument
+    /// ([ADR 0009](../../../docs/adr/0009-performance-guarded-by-shape.md)), not by hand.
+    fn counter_track_for(
+        &mut self,
+        pid: u32,
+        tid: i64,
+        series: &str,
+        metric: &'static str,
+    ) -> Option<u64> {
+        let key = (pid, tid, series.to_string(), metric);
+        if let Some(uuid) = self.counter_tracks.get(&key) {
+            return Some(*uuid);
+        }
+        let (parent, share_key) = if is_top_level(metric) {
+            (self.interpreter_track_for(pid, tid)?, None)
+        } else {
+            (self.counter_group_for(pid, tid)?, Some(metric))
+        };
+
+        let uuid = self.next_uuid;
+        let descriptor = counter_track(
+            uuid,
+            parent,
+            &counter_label(series, metric),
+            metric_rank(metric),
+            share_key,
+        );
+
+        self.file.as_mut()?.write_all(&descriptor).ok()?;
+        self.next_uuid += 1;
+        self.counter_tracks.insert(key, uuid);
+        Some(uuid)
+    }
+
+    /// Draw one sample of every component of a series.
+    ///
+    /// A series is one event and several tracks: `name` is the series and each argument is a
+    /// component of it, which is what decides the tracks rather than anything decided here.
+    ///
+    /// A reading that cannot be a point on this timeline declares **nothing** — not even the
+    /// tracks. There is no pairing to hold together as there is for a slice, so a track drawn
+    /// here would be an empty row standing for a sample gcscope refused to write.
+    fn sample_series(&mut self, pid: u32, tid: i64, ts_ns: i64, series: &str, args: &[Arg]) {
+        let Ok(ts_ns) = u64::try_from(ts_ns) else {
+            self.report_unplaceable(series);
+            return;
+        };
+        for &(metric, value) in args {
+            let Some(uuid) = self.counter_track_for(pid, tid, series, metric) else {
+                continue;
+            };
+            let bytes = counter_sample(uuid, ts_ns, value);
+            if let Some(file) = self.file.as_mut() {
+                file.write_all(&bytes).ok();
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Open a slice on the interpreter's track.
+    ///
+    /// A begin whose timestamp cannot be a point on this timeline is remembered as unwritten
+    /// rather than skipped outright: its `End` is still coming, and an end that closed something
+    /// it did not open would take a slice above it down with it.
+    fn begin_slice(&mut self, pid: u32, tid: i64, ts_ns: i64, name: &str, cat: &str, args: &[Arg]) {
+        let Some(uuid) = self.interpreter_track_for(pid, tid) else {
+            return;
+        };
+        let written = match u64::try_from(ts_ns) {
+            Ok(ts_ns) => {
+                let bytes = slice_begin(uuid, ts_ns, name, cat, args);
+                self.file
+                    .as_mut()
+                    .map(|file| file.write_all(&bytes).is_ok())
+                    .unwrap_or(false)
+            }
+            // `TracePacket.timestamp` is a `uint64`, so a negative sign-extends to roughly 584
+            // years out. A Collection that landed there would look like a measurement.
+            Err(_) => {
+                self.report_unplaceable(name);
+                false
+            }
+        };
+        self.open_slices.entry(uuid).or_default().push(OpenSlice {
+            name: name.to_string(),
+            cat: cat.to_string(),
+            written,
+        });
+    }
+
+    /// Close the innermost slice on the interpreter's track, if it is the one being closed.
+    ///
+    /// The name and category never reach the wire — a `SLICE_END` carries neither — so checking
+    /// them here is the only use they have, and it is the use the event model documents.
+    fn end_slice(&mut self, pid: u32, tid: i64, ts_ns: i64, name: &str, cat: &str) {
+        let Some(uuid) = self.interpreter_tracks.get(&(pid, tid)).copied() else {
+            // Nothing has ever opened on a track that was never declared. Declaring one here to
+            // close a slice on it would draw an empty track for a pairing that is already wrong.
+            //
+            // A write that failed while declaring the track reaches here too, which is why the
+            // warning names that cause as well. Telling the two apart would mean counting the
+            // begins dropped per track, for a disk-full path no test reaches; saying both is
+            // honest and costs nothing. The reachable case — events arriving before `open` — is
+            // dropped whole before this point.
+            self.report_mismatch(name, "no track");
+            return;
+        };
+        let Some(open) = self.open_slices.get_mut(&uuid).and_then(Vec::pop) else {
+            self.report_mismatch(name, "nothing open");
+            return;
+        };
+        if open.name != name || open.cat != cat {
+            // Still closed, and deliberately: Perfetto closes whatever is innermost whatever
+            // this end says, so refusing to write it would leave the slice open and the trace
+            // structurally invalid — a second fault on top of the producer's.
+            self.report_mismatch(name, &open.name);
+        }
+        if !open.written {
+            return;
+        }
+        let Ok(ts_ns) = u64::try_from(ts_ns) else {
+            return;
+        };
+        let bytes = slice_end(uuid, ts_ns);
+        if let Some(file) = self.file.as_mut() {
+            file.write_all(&bytes).ok();
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Say once that a reading could not be a point on this timeline, and keep counting.
+    ///
+    /// `TracePacket.timestamp` is a `uint64`, so a negative would sign-extend to roughly 584 years
+    /// out and read as a measurement. Refusing it is right; refusing it in silence is not. **The
+    /// same `TraceEvent` reaches the Chrome encoder, whose `ts` is signed and takes it**, so a run
+    /// that says nothing here leaves an operator with two traces of one capture that disagree
+    /// about what happened — which is the thing `CombiningExporter` exists to prevent.
+    ///
+    /// The likeliest cause is a `ts_start` resolved through a wrong offset, since a target
+    /// publishes no negative timestamps of its own — the fail-open shape

+    /// number rather than as an error.
+    fn report_unplaceable(&mut self, what: &str) {
+        self.unplaceable += 1;
+        if self.unplaceable == 1 {
+            eprintln!(
+                "warning: \"{what}\" carried a timestamp that is not a point on this timeline, so \
+                 it is missing from the Perfetto trace. A Perfetto timestamp is unsigned; the \
+                 Chrome trace of the same run keeps the reading. The likeliest cause is a Record \
+                 decoded through the wrong offsets. The rest are counted and reported at the end."
+            );
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Say once that a slice did not close what it named, and keep counting.
+    ///
+    /// The likeliest cause is the producer, since everything a [`TraceEvent`] pair says is decided
+    /// in one place — but a descriptor whose write failed reaches here too, and the message names
+    /// both rather than accusing the one it cannot tell apart. Silence would leave a trace that
+    /// reads perfectly well and nests wrongly.
+    fn report_mismatch(&mut self, closing: &str, open: &str) {
+        self.mismatched_ends += 1;
+        if self.mismatched_ends == 1 {
+            eprintln!(
+                "warning: a trace event closed \"{closing}\" while \"{open}\" was what the track \
+                 had open — either the events do not pair or a track could not be written. The \
+                 Perfetto trace nests by what was open, so its slices may not be the ones the \
+                 events described. The rest are counted and reported at the end."
+            );
+        }
+    }
+}

+impl EventsExporter for PerfettoExporter {
+    /// `.json` is the one extension this format must not keep — a file holding protobuf under
+    /// it is one nobody opens twice — so that one is replaced. Anything else is **appended**
+    /// to rather than replaced: `-o capture.2026-08-09` is a name an operator chose, not a
+    /// claim about the format, and replacing it would fold two days' captures into one file.
+    fn output_path(&self, requested: &Path) -> PathBuf {
+        let extension = requested
+            .extension()
+            .and_then(|extension| extension.to_str())
+            .unwrap_or_default();
+
+        let mut path = requested.to_path_buf();
+        if extension.eq_ignore_ascii_case(EXTENSION) {
+            return path;
+        }
+        if extension.eq_ignore_ascii_case("json") {
+            path.set_extension(EXTENSION);
+            return path;
+        }
+
+        let mut name = path.file_name().unwrap_or_default().to_os_string();
+        name.push(".");
+        name.push(EXTENSION);
+        path.set_file_name(name);
+        path
+    }
+
+    fn open(&mut self, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
+            .create(true)
+            .truncate(true)
+            .write(true)
+            .open(path)?;
+
+        // Written here rather than before the first event, so a run that saw nothing still
+        // produces a trace a reader opens instead of a zero-byte file. The snapshot leads,
+        // because it is what every timestamp after it is read through.
+        file.write_all(&clock_snapshot_packet(&self.run))?;
+        file.write_all(&root_descriptor())?;
+        file.flush()?;
+
+        self.file = Some(file);
+        self.process_tracks.clear();
+        self.marked_started.clear();
+        self.interpreter_tracks.clear();
+        self.counter_groups.clear();
+        self.counter_tracks.clear();
+        // The open slices go with them. A reopened file is a new trace, and a slice opened into
+        // the old one has no end coming that this file could write — carried over, it would let
+        // the next end close something this file never opened.
+        self.open_slices.clear();
+        // The tallies belong to a trace, not to the exporter. Carried over, the second file's
+        // first mismatch goes unreported — the "say it once" guard has already fired — and its
+        // closing count is another file's.
+        self.mismatched_ends = 0;
+        self.unplaceable = 0;
+        self.next_uuid = FIRST_TRACK_UUID;
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    /// The metadata arms run whether or not there is a file to write to. `track_for` writes
+    /// nothing and consumes nothing without one, and the names have to be recorded either way: a
+    /// batch that arrives before `open` is dropped, but the announcement it carried is the only
+    /// one that process or interpreter gets.
+    ///
+    /// The slice arms are guarded, because a pair is only meaningful whole.
+    fn add_events(&mut self, events: &[TraceEvent]) {
+        for event in events {
+            match event {
+                // Remembered before the write and kept whether or not it succeeds. A descriptor
+                // that has to be written again — no file yet, or a write that failed — must not
+                // lose the name with it, because no second announcement is coming.
+                TraceEvent::ProcessMeta { pid, name } => {
+                    self.process_names.insert(*pid, name.clone());
+                    self.track_for(*pid);
+                }
+                TraceEvent::ThreadMeta { pid, tid, name } => {
+                    self.interpreter_names.insert((*pid, *tid), name.clone());
+                    self.interpreter_track_for(*pid, *tid);
+                }
+                // Both halves are skipped together while there is no file. A `Begin` dropped for
+                // want of one is not a pairing fault, and letting its `End` through would report
+                // the batch that arrived early as a producer bug.
+                TraceEvent::Begin {
+                    pid,
+                    tid,
+                    ts_ns,
+                    name,
+                    cat,
+                    args,
+                } if self.file.is_some() => self.begin_slice(*pid, *tid, *ts_ns, name, cat, args),
+                TraceEvent::End {
+                    pid,
+                    tid,
+                    ts_ns,
+                    name,
+                    cat,
+                } if self.file.is_some() => self.end_slice(*pid, *tid, *ts_ns, name, cat),
+                TraceEvent::Begin { .. } | TraceEvent::End { .. } => {}
+                // Unguarded, unlike the pair above: a sample stands on its own, so one dropped
+                // for want of a file leaves nothing half-done behind it. Without one, every
+                // declaration below writes nothing and consumes nothing.
+                TraceEvent::Counter {
+                    pid,
+                    tid,
+                    ts_ns,
+                    name,
+                    args,
+                } => self.sample_series(*pid, *tid, *ts_ns, name, args),
+                // Nothing produces an `Instant` yet, and it is dropped rather than encoded as
+                // something plausible: the control plane that would inject one is not built.
+                TraceEvent::Instant { .. } => {}
+            }
+        }
+        if let Some(file) = self.file.as_mut() {
+            file.flush().ok();
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// `Started` draws the marker that keeps the process visible; `Died` draws nothing yet.
+    ///
+    /// Without a reading there is no marker. An instant has to sit somewhere on the timeline,
+    /// and a zero puts it at the origin — decades from the rest of the trace, and read as a
+    /// measurement by anyone who does not know it was a placeholder.
+    fn mark_process_lifecycle(&mut self, pid: u32, kind: ProcessLifecycle, ts_ns: Option<i64>) {
+        let ProcessLifecycle::Started = kind else {
+            return;
+        };
+        // The track first, and **before the readings are examined**. The mark can arrive before
+        // the announcement that names the process — an event on a track nothing declared is what
+        // the harness's checks reject — and a process gcscope has no reading for still belongs in
+        // the trace. A descriptor alone reaches trace-processor's `process` table, so an operator
+        // sees the worker listed even where there is no marker to draw on it.
+        let Some(uuid) = self.track_for(pid) else {
+            return;
+        };
+        let Some(ts_ns) = ts_ns else {
+            return;
+        };
+        // The reading is already on the machine's monotonic clock — the one CPython published its
+        // own timestamps on — so it is placed exactly as a Collection's is. There is nothing to
+        // rebase, which is what puts this marker and the Collections that follow on one timeline.
+        //
+        // `TracePacket.timestamp` is a `uint64`. A negative reading is not a point on this
+        // timeline — written out it sign-extends to roughly 584 years — so it is refused here
+        // rather than placed somewhere absurd, which is the whole of ADR 0022.
+        let Ok(ts_ns) = u64::try_from(ts_ns) else {
+            return;
+        };
+        if self.marked_started.contains(&pid) {
+            return;
+        }
+        let Some(file) = self.file.as_mut() else {
+            return;
+        };
+        if file.write_all(&start_process_instant(uuid, ts_ns)).is_ok() {
+            self.marked_started.insert(pid);
+        }
+        file.flush().ok();
+    }
+
+    fn close(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
+        // Nothing terminates a Perfetto trace — the file is its packets — so closing is
+        // flushing and letting the handle go. `run_loop` unwinds through `close` on paths
+        // where `open` never ran, and closing twice has to be as harmless.
+        if self.mismatched_ends > 1 {
+            eprintln!(
+                "warning: {} trace events in all closed a slice other than the one their track \
+                 had open.",
+                self.mismatched_ends
+            );
+        }
+        if self.unplaceable > 1 {
+            eprintln!(
+                "warning: {} trace events in all carried a timestamp this format cannot hold, \
+                 and are missing from the trace.",
+                self.unplaceable
+            );
+        }
+        let Some(mut file) = self.file.take() else {
+            return Ok(());
+        };
+        file.flush()
+    }

+    /// Whether these bytes are a sequence of complete `Trace.packet` fields and nothing else.
+    /// A cheap structural proxy for the real decoder in `tests/perfetto_encoder.rs`: it catches
+    /// a length prefix that disagrees with what follows it, which is how a truncated or
+    /// double-counted submessage shows up.
+    fn packet_lengths(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<usize>> {
+        let mut lengths = Vec::new();
+        let mut rest = bytes;
+        while !rest.is_empty() {
+            // Field 1, wire type 2 — the only field a `Trace` has.
+            if rest[0] != 0x0a {
+                return None;
+            }
+            let mut length = 0usize;
+            let mut shift = 0;
+            let mut index = 1;
+            loop {
+                let byte = *rest.get(index)?;
+                length |= usize::from(byte & 0x7f) << shift;
+                index += 1;
+                if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
+                    break;
+                }
+                shift += 7;
+            }
+            if rest.len() < index + length {
+                return None;
+            }
+            lengths.push(length);
+            rest = &rest[index + length..];
+        }
+        Some(lengths)
+    }

+    // Byte-for-byte gate.
+    //
+    // Ascending field order and a fixed sequence id are decisions this file states, and they
+    // are what makes one input produce one byte sequence. Nothing else pins them: the tests

+    //
+    // What the bytes say, read left to right. The clock snapshot first, on [`fixed_clock`]:
+    //   0a 12                Trace.packet (field 1, length-delimited), 18 bytes
+    //     32 0e              TracePacket.clock_snapshot (6), 14 bytes
+    //       0a 05            ClockSnapshot.clocks (1), 5 bytes
+    //         08 06          Clock.clock_id (1) = 6, BUILTIN_CLOCK_BOOTTIME
+    //         10 a8 46       Clock.timestamp (2) = 9000
+    //       0a 05            .clocks again, 5 bytes
+    //         08 40          Clock.clock_id = 64, gcscope's own domain
+    //         10 88 27       Clock.timestamp = 5000
+    //     50 01              TracePacket.trusted_packet_sequence_id (10) = 1
+    // and the root descriptor after it:
+    //   0a 0d                Trace.packet, 13 bytes
+    //     50 01              trusted_packet_sequence_id = 1
+    //     e2 03 08           TracePacket.track_descriptor (60), 8 bytes
+    //       08 00            TrackDescriptor.uuid (1) = 0, the root
+    //       98 01 01         .process_ordering (19) = PROCESS_ORDERING_EXPLICIT
+    //       a0 01 01         .thread_ordering (20) = THREAD_ORDERING_EXPLICIT
+    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    const CLOCK_SNAPSHOT_BYTES: [u8; 20] = [
+        0x0a, 0x12, 0x32, 0x0e, 0x0a, 0x05, 0x08, 0x06, 0x10, 0xa8, 0x46, 0x0a, 0x05, 0x08, 0x40,
+        0x10, 0x88, 0x27, 0x50, 0x01,
+    ];
+
+    const ROOT_DESCRIPTOR_BYTES: [u8; 15] = [
+        0x0a, 0x0d, 0x50, 0x01, 0xe2, 0x03, 0x08, 0x08, 0x00, 0x98, 0x01, 0x01, 0xa0, 0x01, 0x01,
+    ];
+
+    /// The two packets every trace opens with, in the order it opens with them.
+    fn preamble_bytes() -> Vec<u8> {
+        CLOCK_SNAPSHOT_BYTES
+            .iter()
+            .chain(&ROOT_DESCRIPTOR_BYTES)
+            .copied()
+            .collect()
+    }

+    ///       08 01            uuid = 1
+    ///       12 0b …          .name (2) = "python 4242"
+    ///       1a 10            .process (3), 16 bytes
+    ///         08 92 21       ProcessDescriptor.pid (1) = 4242
+    ///         32 0b …        .process_name (6) = "python 4242"

+    /// a field that is present and reads zero puts the sub-span's start before its parent's. The
+    /// encoder writes what it was handed rather than sorting it back into shape: the raw numbers
+    /// are what the target published, and a reordering here would invent a pause that never ran.
+    #[test]
+    fn a_sub_span_before_its_parent_is_written_in_the_order_it_arrived() {
+        let mut exporter = exporter();
+        let path = temp_path();
+        exporter.open(&path).unwrap();
+        exporter.add_events(&[
+            process_meta(1),
+            thread_meta(1, 0),
+            TraceEvent::Begin {
+                pid: 1,
+                tid: 0,
+                ts_ns: 60_000,
+                name: "GC Pause (gen=0)".to_string(),
+                cat: "gc.pause(gen=0)".to_string(),
+                args: vec![],
+            },
+            // Chained onto a `ts_handle_weakref_callbacks_stop` its build defines and never
+            // wrote, so it begins at the epoch — before the pause enclosing it.
+            TraceEvent::Begin {
+                pid: 1,
+                tid: 0,
+                ts_ns: 0,
+                name: "Finalize Garbage (gen=0)".to_string(),
+                cat: "gc.finalize(gen=0)".to_string(),
+                args: vec![],
+            },
+            TraceEvent::End {
+                pid: 1,
+                tid: 0,
+                ts_ns: 65_000,
+                name: "Finalize Garbage (gen=0)".to_string(),
+                cat: "gc.finalize(gen=0)".to_string(),
+            },
+            TraceEvent::End {
+                pid: 1,
+                tid: 0,
+                ts_ns: 70_000,
+                name: "GC Pause (gen=0)".to_string(),
+                cat: "gc.pause(gen=0)".to_string(),
+            },
+        ]);
+        exporter.close().unwrap();
+        let bytes = fs::read(&path).unwrap();
+        fs::remove_file(&path).ok();

+        assert_eq!(packet_count(&bytes), PREAMBLE + 6);
+        assert_eq!(exporter.mismatched_ends, 0, "the pair still matches");
+    }

+    /// A `SLICE_END` carries no name, so the name an `End` repeats can only ever be checked.

+    /// An end for a track that never opened anything writes nothing. Written, it would be an end

+    /// The per-generation series as the conversion emits one.
+    fn metrics(pid: u32, tid: i64, ts_ns: i64, generation: u32) -> TraceEvent {

+            tid,

+//! Perfetto's field numbers and enum values, and nothing else.
+//!
+//! Transcribed by hand from Perfetto's `.proto` files, which is only safe because the test
+//! travels with the table: `tests/perfetto_encoder.rs` hands [`FIELDS`] and [`ENUM_VALUES`] to
+//! `tests/harness/proto_constants.py`, which reads each number back out of the official
+//! generated descriptors. A wrong number here writes a *different* message rather than an
+//! invalid one, so nothing in gcscope's own output can catch it — see
+//! [ADR 0021](../../../docs/adr/0021-hand-rolled-perfetto-encoder.md).
+//!
+//! **Both tables are built by the macros below from the same declarations that define the
+//! constants.** That is deliberate: a constant added without an assertion line is the failure
+//! this file guards against, so there is no way to declare one that stays out of the list the
+//! checker is given. Adding a field means adding one line, and the line carries its own proof.
+//!
+//! Numbers are not in ascending order within a message. They are grouped as Perfetto's
+//! `.proto` groups them, and the gaps are real — a later field number does not mean a later
+//! addition.
+
+macro_rules! proto_messages {
+    ($(
+        $(#[$message_doc:meta])*
+        $module:ident = $message:literal {
+            $(
+                $(#[$field_doc:meta])*
+                $konst:ident = $number:literal as $field:literal,
+            )*
+        }
+    )*) => {
+        $(
+            $(#[$message_doc])*
+            pub mod $module {
+                $(
+                    $(#[$field_doc])*
+                    pub const $konst: u32 = $number;
+                )*
+            }
+        )*
+
+        /// Every field number above, as `(message, field, number)`, for the descriptor check.
+        pub const FIELDS: &[(&str, &str, u32)] = &[
+            $($( ($message, $field, $module::$konst), )*)*
+        ];
+    };
+}
+
+macro_rules! proto_enums {
+    ($(
+        $(#[$enum_doc:meta])*
+        $module:ident = $message:literal . $enum_name:literal {
+            $(
+                $(#[$value_doc:meta])*
+                $konst:ident = $number:literal as $value:literal,
+            )*
+        }
+    )*) => {
+        $(
+            $(#[$enum_doc])*
+            pub mod $module {
+                $(
+                    $(#[$value_doc])*
+                    pub const $konst: u32 = $number;
+                )*
+            }
+        )*
+
+        /// Every enum value above, as `(message, enum, value, number)`, for the same check.
+        pub const ENUM_VALUES: &[(&str, &str, &str, u32)] = &[
+            $($( ($message, $enum_name, $value, $module::$konst), )*)*
+        ];
+    };
+}
+
+proto_messages! {
+    /// The whole file: a `Trace` is a repeated `TracePacket` and nothing else, which is what
+    /// lets an encoder append packets to an open file instead of building the trace in memory.
+    trace = "Trace" {
+        PACKET = 1 as "packet",
+    }
+
+    /// The envelope every event travels in.
+    trace_packet = "TracePacket" {
+        /// Where a timestamp goes. **Never** inside `TrackEvent`: field 1 there is
+        /// `timestamp_delta_us`, so an absolute nanosecond stamp written into a `TrackEvent`
+        /// decodes as a microsecond delta and lands the event somewhere else entirely.
+        TIMESTAMP = 8 as "timestamp",
+        /// Which clock the `timestamp` beside it is on. Absent means the trace's own, which is
+        /// BOOTTIME — a claim gcscope cannot make about a counter it read out of CPython, so
+        /// every packet carrying a timestamp names its domain here instead.
+        TIMESTAMP_CLOCK_ID = 58 as "timestamp_clock_id",
+        /// Required in practice. Perfetto drops packets that name no sequence, since
+        /// interning and incremental state are sequence-scoped.
+        TRUSTED_PACKET_SEQUENCE_ID = 10 as "trusted_packet_sequence_id",
+        TRACK_EVENT = 11 as "track_event",
+        CLOCK_SNAPSHOT = 6 as "clock_snapshot",
+        TRACK_DESCRIPTOR = 60 as "track_descriptor",

+    /// Ties a producer's clock to one the reader knows, so events stamped in the producer's
+    /// domain can be converted into trace time.
+    clock_snapshot = "ClockSnapshot" {
+        CLOCKS = 1 as "clocks",
+        /// Which builtin clock trace time is measured in. gcscope leaves it unset and takes
+        /// the default, BOOTTIME, which is what the snapshot below anchors against.
+        PRIMARY_TRACE_CLOCK = 2 as "primary_trace_clock",
+    }
+
+    /// One clock's reading inside a [`clock_snapshot`]. Nested inside `ClockSnapshot`, which is
+    /// why the checker is handed the path rather than the bare name.
+    clock = "ClockSnapshot.Clock" {
+        CLOCK_ID = 1 as "clock_id",
+        TIMESTAMP = 2 as "timestamp",
+        IS_INCREMENTAL = 3 as "is_incremental",
+        UNIT_MULTIPLIER_NS = 4 as "unit_multiplier_ns",
+    }
+
+    /// Declares a track: a row in the UI, and the thing every event names.
+    track_descriptor = "TrackDescriptor" {
+        UUID = 1 as "uuid",
+        NAME = 2 as "name",
+        PROCESS = 3 as "process",
+        THREAD = 4 as "thread",
+        PARENT_UUID = 5 as "parent_uuid",
+        COUNTER = 8 as "counter",
+        CHILD_ORDERING = 11 as "child_ordering",
+        SIBLING_ORDER_RANK = 12 as "sibling_order_rank",
+        DESCRIPTION = 14 as "description",
+        PROCESS_ORDERING = 19 as "process_ordering",
+        THREAD_ORDERING = 20 as "thread_ordering",
+    }
+
+    thread_descriptor = "ThreadDescriptor" {
+        PID = 1 as "pid",
+        TID = 2 as "tid",
+        THREAD_NAME = 5 as "thread_name",
+    }
+
+    process_descriptor = "ProcessDescriptor" {
+        PID = 1 as "pid",
+        CMDLINE = 2 as "cmdline",
+        PROCESS_NAME = 6 as "process_name",
+        START_TIMESTAMP_NS = 7 as "start_timestamp_ns",
+    }
+
+    counter_descriptor = "CounterDescriptor" {
+        TYPE = 1 as "type",
+        CATEGORIES = 2 as "categories",
+        UNIT = 3 as "unit",
+        UNIT_MULTIPLIER = 4 as "unit_multiplier",
+        IS_INCREMENTAL = 5 as "is_incremental",
+        UNIT_NAME = 6 as "unit_name",
+        Y_AXIS_SHARE_KEY = 7 as "y_axis_share_key",
+    }
+
+    track_event = "TrackEvent" {
+        TYPE = 9 as "type",
+        TRACK_UUID = 11 as "track_uuid",
+        DEBUG_ANNOTATIONS = 4 as "debug_annotations",
+        CATEGORIES = 22 as "categories",
+        NAME = 23 as "name",
+        COUNTER_VALUE = 30 as "counter_value",
+        DOUBLE_COUNTER_VALUE = 44 as "double_counter_value",
+        /// Listed so the two timestamp fields that must stay empty are named somewhere a
+        /// reader will find them. gcscope writes neither: see `trace_packet::TIMESTAMP`.
+        TIMESTAMP_DELTA_US = 1 as "timestamp_delta_us",
+        TIMESTAMP_ABSOLUTE_US = 16 as "timestamp_absolute_us",
+    }
+
+    debug_annotation = "DebugAnnotation" {
+        /// **Field 10, not field 1, and it looks like a typo.** The proto declares
+        /// `oneof name_field { uint64 name_iid = 1; string name = 10; }`. Only one member of a
+        /// oneof may be set, and field 1 is the interned id, so a string written there is read
+        /// as a garbage IID that can collide with a real interned name. Do not "fix" this to 1.
+        NAME = 10 as "name",
+        BOOL_VALUE = 2 as "bool_value",
+        INT_VALUE = 4 as "int_value",
+        DOUBLE_VALUE = 5 as "double_value",
+        STRING_VALUE = 6 as "string_value",
+    }
+}
+
+proto_enums! {
+    track_event_type = "TrackEvent"."Type" {
+        SLICE_BEGIN = 1 as "TYPE_SLICE_BEGIN",
+        SLICE_END = 2 as "TYPE_SLICE_END",
+        INSTANT = 3 as "TYPE_INSTANT",
+        COUNTER = 4 as "TYPE_COUNTER",
+    }
+
+    /// How a track's children are arranged under it.
+    child_tracks_ordering = "TrackDescriptor"."ChildTracksOrdering" {
+        UNKNOWN = 0 as "UNKNOWN",
+        LEXICOGRAPHIC = 1 as "LEXICOGRAPHIC",
+        CHRONOLOGICAL = 2 as "CHRONOLOGICAL",
+        EXPLICIT = 3 as "EXPLICIT",
+    }
+
+    /// How top-level process tracks are arranged. Only meaningful on the root descriptor.
+    process_ordering = "TrackDescriptor"."ProcessOrdering" {
+        UNSPECIFIED = 0 as "PROCESS_ORDERING_UNSPECIFIED",
+        EXPLICIT = 1 as "PROCESS_ORDERING_EXPLICIT",
+    }
+
+    /// The clock domains a reader already knows. Declared at file scope rather than inside a
+    /// message, which is what the empty scope spells: there is no `BuiltinClock` message to
+    /// hang it off, and the checker resolves it from the file's own enums.
+    ///
+    /// Only `BOOTTIME` is written. The other two are here because they are what an anchor
+    /// *looks* like it could use and cannot: a snapshot naming either leaves trace-processor
+    /// with no path from gcscope's domain to trace time, so it reports
+    /// `clock_sync_failure_no_path` and drops every event
+    /// ([ADR 0022](../../../docs/adr/0022-every-timestamp-names-its-clock.md)).
+    builtin_clock = ""."BuiltinClock" {
+        REALTIME = 1 as "BUILTIN_CLOCK_REALTIME",
+        MONOTONIC = 3 as "BUILTIN_CLOCK_MONOTONIC",
+        BOOTTIME = 6 as "BUILTIN_CLOCK_BOOTTIME",
+        /// The last id reserved for a builtin. gcscope's own domain has to be above it, and
+        /// this is what says so rather than a number chosen for looking large enough.
+        MAX_ID = 63 as "BUILTIN_CLOCK_MAX_ID",
+    }
+
+    thread_ordering = "TrackDescriptor"."ThreadOrdering" {
+        UNSPECIFIED = 0 as "THREAD_ORDERING_UNSPECIFIED",
+        EXPLICIT = 1 as "THREAD_ORDERING_EXPLICIT",
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    /// The tables are what the checker is handed, and an empty one passes every check in it.
+    /// The declarations and the table entries come from the same macro arm, so this asks only
+    /// whether that arm is still collecting — the numbers themselves are the descriptors' to
+    /// confirm, not this test's.
+    #[test]
+    fn the_declarations_reach_the_tables_the_checker_reads() {
+        assert!(FIELDS.contains(&("DebugAnnotation", "name", 10)));
+        assert!(FIELDS.contains(&("Trace", "packet", 1)));
+        assert!(FIELDS.contains(&("ClockSnapshot.Clock", "clock_id", 1)));
+        assert!(ENUM_VALUES.contains(&("", "BuiltinClock", "BUILTIN_CLOCK_BOOTTIME", 6)));
+        assert!(ENUM_VALUES.contains(&("TrackEvent", "Type", "TYPE_SLICE_BEGIN", 1)));
+        assert!(ENUM_VALUES.contains(&(
+            "TrackDescriptor",
+            "ProcessOrdering",
+            "PROCESS_ORDERING_EXPLICIT",
+            1
+        )));
+    }
+
+    /// Inside one message, a field name and a field number each belong to one constant. Two
+    /// constants sharing either would both pass the descriptor check while the code reads only
+    /// one of them, which is how a copied line goes unnoticed.
+    #[test]
+    fn no_message_claims_a_field_or_a_number_twice() {
+        for (index, first) in FIELDS.iter().enumerate() {
+            for second in &FIELDS[index + 1..] {
+                assert!(
+                    !(first.0 == second.0 && (first.1 == second.1 || first.2 == second.2)),
+                    "{first:?} and {second:?} claim the same field or the same number"
+                );
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The one constant whose correct value reads as a mistake. Pinned here as well as against
+    /// the descriptors, so a "fix" back to 1 fails in the crate that made it rather than only
+    /// on the leg with the `perfetto` package installed.
+    #[test]
+    fn a_debug_annotation_names_itself_at_field_ten() {
+        assert_eq!(debug_annotation::NAME, 10);
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,199 @@
+//! A write-only protobuf wire encoder: enough of the format to write a Perfetto trace, and no
+//! more. There is no reader here and no schema — a caller names the field number and the type
+//! it means, and these functions append the bytes.
+//!
+//! Hand-rolled rather than generated, for the reason
+//! [ADR 0021](../../../docs/adr/0021-hand-rolled-perfetto-encoder.md) gives. The half of that
+//! decision that makes it safe lives outside this file: everything written here is decoded
+//! back by the `perfetto` package in `tests/perfetto_encoder.rs`, because a wrong varint fails
+//! **open** — it produces a file that parses to a different number, not one that fails to
+//! parse.
+//!
+//! Two rules the wire format imposes that are easy to get backwards:
+//!
+//! - A negative `int32` or `int64` is written **sign-extended to 64 bits**, so it always takes
+//!   ten bytes. gcmon masked to 32 bits and wrote `sibling_order_rank = -1` as `0`, which
+//!   parses fine and reorders the UI.
+//! - A submessage is its own encoded body, written as a length-delimited field. Nothing
+//!   distinguishes it on the wire from a `bytes` field, so [`put_message`] and [`put_bytes`]
+//!   emit the same shape; they are separate names so a reader sees which one was meant.
+
+/// Wire type 0: `int32`, `int64`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `bool`, and enums.
+pub const WIRE_VARINT: u32 = 0;
+/// Wire type 1: `fixed64`, `sfixed64`, `double`.
+pub const WIRE_FIXED64: u32 = 1;
+/// Wire type 2: `string`, `bytes`, embedded messages, packed repeated fields.
+pub const WIRE_LENGTH_DELIMITED: u32 = 2;
+
+/// A base-128 varint, least-significant group first, continuation bit on every byte but the
+/// last. Zero is one byte, not none.
+pub fn put_varint(out: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: u64) {
+    while value >= 0x80 {
+        out.push((value as u8) | 0x80);
+        value >>= 7;
+    }
+    out.push(value as u8);
+}
+
+/// The tag that opens a field: its number and the wire type of what follows.
+pub fn put_key(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, wire_type: u32) {
+    put_varint(out, u64::from((field << 3) | wire_type));
+}
+
+/// A `uint64`/`uint32`/`bool` field, or an enum whose value is not negative.
+pub fn put_uint64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, value: u64) {
+    put_key(out, field, WIRE_VARINT);
+    put_varint(out, value);
+}
+
+/// An `int64` field. Negatives are sign-extended, per the wire format.
+pub fn put_int64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, value: i64) {
+    put_uint64(out, field, value as u64);
+}
+
+/// An `int32` field. Negatives are sign-extended to **64** bits — the width of the varint does
+/// not follow the width of the declared type, and truncating to 32 writes a large positive
+/// number instead.
+pub fn put_int32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, value: i32) {
+    put_int64(out, field, i64::from(value));
+}
+
+/// A `double` field: IEEE-754 bits, little-endian, always eight bytes.
+pub fn put_double(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, value: f64) {
+    put_key(out, field, WIRE_FIXED64);
+    out.extend_from_slice(&value.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
+}
+
+/// A length-delimited field carrying raw bytes.
+pub fn put_bytes(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, value: &[u8]) {
+    put_key(out, field, WIRE_LENGTH_DELIMITED);
+    put_varint(out, value.len() as u64);
+    out.extend_from_slice(value);
+}
+
+/// A `string` field. Rust strings are already UTF-8, which is what the wire format wants.
+pub fn put_string(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, value: &str) {
+    put_bytes(out, field, value.as_bytes());
+}
+
+/// A submessage, given its encoded body. An empty body is still written: a field present with
+/// length zero is how "this message exists and is empty" is spelled, and omitting it says
+/// something else.
+pub fn put_message(out: &mut Vec<u8>, field: u32, body: &[u8]) {
+    put_bytes(out, field, body);
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    fn varint(value: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_varint(&mut out, value);
+        out
+    }
+
+    /// The boundaries, where a shift-by-seven loop goes wrong: zero must be one byte rather
+    /// than none, and each multiple of seven bits adds one.
+    #[test]
+    fn a_varint_grows_one_byte_every_seven_bits() {
+        assert_eq!(varint(0), [0x00]);
+        assert_eq!(varint(1), [0x01]);
+        assert_eq!(varint(127), [0x7f]);
+        assert_eq!(varint(128), [0x80, 0x01]);
+        assert_eq!(varint(300), [0xac, 0x02]);
+        assert_eq!(
+            varint(u64::MAX),
+            [0xff; 9].iter().chain(&[0x01]).copied().collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        );
+    }
+
+    /// A field key is the number shifted three places with the wire type below it. Field 60 is
+    /// `TracePacket.track_descriptor`, past the one-byte boundary, so a key that is itself a
+    /// multi-byte varint is covered.
+    #[test]
+    fn a_field_key_carries_the_number_and_the_wire_type() {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_key(&mut out, 1, WIRE_LENGTH_DELIMITED);
+        assert_eq!(out, [0x0a]);
+
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_key(&mut out, 60, WIRE_LENGTH_DELIMITED);
+        assert_eq!(out, [0xe2, 0x03]);
+    }
+
+    /// The bug this file's header names: a negative written as an `int32` occupies ten bytes,
+    /// because the varint is sign-extended to 64 bits regardless of the declared width. Masking
+    /// to 32 bits produces a valid varint holding the wrong number.
+    #[test]
+    fn a_negative_int32_is_sign_extended_to_ten_bytes() {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_int32(&mut out, 12, -1);
+        assert_eq!(
+            out,
+            [
+                0x60, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x01
+            ]
+        );
+
+        let mut masked = Vec::new();
+        put_varint(&mut masked, u64::from((-1i32) as u32));
+        assert_eq!(masked.len(), 5, "what truncating to 32 bits would write");
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn i64_min_and_max_survive_as_int64() {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_int64(&mut out, 1, i64::MIN);
+        assert_eq!(out.len(), 11, "key plus a ten-byte varint");
+
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_int64(&mut out, 1, i64::MAX);
+        assert_eq!(
+            out,
+            [0x08, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x7f]
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_double_is_eight_little_endian_bytes() {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_double(&mut out, 44, 1.0);
+        assert_eq!(
+            out,
+            [0xe1, 0x02, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xf0, 0x3f]
+        );
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn a_string_is_its_length_then_its_utf8() {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_string(&mut out, 2, "GC");
+        assert_eq!(out, [0x12, 0x02, b'G', b'C']);
+
+        // Length is in bytes, not characters, so a multi-byte one must not read as one.
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_string(&mut out, 2, "é");
+        assert_eq!(out, [0x12, 0x02, 0xc3, 0xa9]);
+    }
+
+    /// An empty submessage is a field with length zero, not an absent field. It is how a
+    /// descriptor says "this process has no attributes I know" while still declaring one.
+    #[test]
+    fn an_empty_message_is_written_rather_than_skipped() {
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_message(&mut out, 3, &[]);
+        assert_eq!(out, [0x1a, 0x00]);
+    }
+
+    /// Nesting is length-prefixing: the body is encoded first, then written whole.
+    #[test]
+    fn a_submessage_carries_its_bodys_length() {
+        let mut body = Vec::new();
+        put_uint64(&mut body, 1, 4242);
+
+        let mut out = Vec::new();
+        put_message(&mut out, 3, &body);
+        assert_eq!(out, [0x1a, 0x03, 0x08, 0x92, 0x21]);
+    }
+}
